clue.text: Ditch has to be found in county

indicators.note: to be found in something is to sit inside it, so these letters go within the county

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland
'is' is a form of the verb to be

explanation.surface: A ditch needing to be found somewhere in a rural county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditch' looks like a noun for a trench, but here it is a verb meaning to reject.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch someone is to cast them off or repudiate them, a close synonym.

clue.text: One locked up by judge for unholy crime?

indicators.note: something locked up by another is enclosed inside it, so the numeral sits within the verb

parts.note: to judge a matter is to decide it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone imprisoned by a judge for a wicked offence.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'unholy crime' is a playful way of describing the murder of a god.
explanation.definitionFit: Killing a deity is about as irreligious an offence as can be imagined, hence an unholy crime.

clue.text: As De Niro might say, 'Take a seat' in an old chair

indicators.note: the actor's New York drawl is imagined pronouncing an instruction, so the clue is about how the words sound

parts.note: an invitation to sit down, which in a New York accent comes out roughly as 'siddan'

explanation.surface: An actor offering someone a seat in an antique chair.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert De Niro's New York delivery of 'sit down' is caricatured as 'siddan', which is how the answer is pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan chair was an enclosed seat carried on poles, a vehicle of the eighteenth century.

clue.text: Show how novel is biographical reference

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of the two words are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Showing how a novel counts as a biographical reference work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the noun for a book, but it is the adjective new, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the annual directory of short biographies of notable living people.

clue.text: Standard requirements on application form reversed for wine seller

indicators.note: reversed tells us the pair of form fields is read from the end back to the start

parts.note: forms routinely ask for your age and your DOB, date of birth

explanation.surface: A wine merchant filling in an application form backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine shop or cellar, so a seller of wine.

clue.text: Demanding love, Gloriana entertained by wit

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is taken in, so the queen sits inside the word for wit

parts.note: nous is common sense or wit
Gloriana was a poetic name for Elizabeth I, Elizabeth Regina, ER

explanation.surface: A demanding romance in which Queen Elizabeth is amused by a witty courtier.
explanation.walkthrough: Gloriana was Spenser's name for Elizabeth I; ER stands for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A demanding task is burdensome and taxing, which is what onerous means.

clue.text: Cooler, retired agricultural worker?

parts.note: ex means former, as of someone retired from a post
a tractor does the heavy work on a farm

explanation.surface: A retired farmhand who is cooler than the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agricultural worker' looks like a farm labourer, but here it is a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: An extractor fan draws out hot air and steam, cooling a kitchen or bathroom.

clue.text: Ringed zone around old lake and river

indicators.note: around means the zone surrounds the abbreviations that follow

parts.note: a zone is an area
L abbreviates lake on maps
R abbreviates river on maps

explanation.surface: A ringed zone surrounding an old lake and its river, like a map feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringed zone' reads as a phrase, but the definition is just the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Areolar describes having an areola, a small circular ring, so it means ringed or circled.

clue.text: Where accessory may be left in the gap that's up the wall

indicators.note: up the wall means crazy or distraught, so the letters are in a mad jumble

explanation.surface: A spot in a gap high on the wall where a fashion item can be hung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up the wall' looks like a location for a peg, but it is the slang for going crazy, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat is an accessory, and a wall-mounted peg is where it is hung on arrival.

clue.text: Peas in a pod hard when served with roast beef, if out to lunch

indicators.note: out to lunch is slang for crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Peas served hard alongside roast beef, if the cook is distracted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peas in a pod' seems to be a vegetable in the meal, but it is the idiom for two very similar people.
explanation.definitionFit: Both idioms describe people who are alike; similar types are said to flock together.

clue.text: Nobody has time at the moment

parts.note: MIN, short for minute, is a unit of time
at the moment means now

explanation.surface: Nobody has any time to spare right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nobody' reads as no person, but it is the noun for an insignificant one.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fish is a common figure for a person of no importance, a nonentity.

clue.text: Chances are minimal in the end, very young earner has admitted?

parts.note: a pro, a professional, is someone who earns from their activity

indicators.note: something admitted is let in, so the letter goes inside the word for an infant

parts.note: a baby is very young

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of minimal

explanation.surface: The odds are slim that a very young wage earner has confessed something.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'chances are' signals that something is likely, just as the adverb does.

clue.text: Politician always backward-looking, noxious air nauseating, ultimately

indicators.note: backward-looking means the poetic word for always is read from end to start

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always
smog is polluted, harmful air

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of nauseating

explanation.surface: A dig at a politician seen as backward-looking and full of nauseating hot air.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacob Rees-Mogg is a British Conservative MP known for old-fashioned manners, which the surface teases.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob Rees-Mogg is a Conservative MP and former cabinet minister.

clue.text: Where ships are in peril, Pacific port offers sanctuary to sailor

indicators.note: giving sanctuary means taking someone in, so the sailor goes inside the city

parts.note: Seattle is a port on the US Pacific coast
AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A Pacific harbour city sheltering a sailor from ships in danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Naval combat is a situation where vessels face being sunk.

clue.text: Where Cassini ended mission, go beyond it

indicators.note: beyond places the word for go after the letters for it

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal, SA
a turn is a go, as in a game

explanation.surface: A space probe's final mission, and the challenge to go further.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cassini probe ended its mission in 2017 by diving into the ringed planet it had orbited.
explanation.definitionFit: NASA's Cassini spacecraft was deliberately plunged into this planet's atmosphere to end its mission.

clue.text: Headline story from page penned by hack

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, as in a pen, so the page letter sits inside

parts.note: to hack is to slash or cut

explanation.surface: A lead news story written by a hack journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by hack' suggests a journalist writing, but 'penned' means enclosed and 'hack' means cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash is newspaper slang for the main front-page story.

clue.text: Might one wish to warm fingers up in scaling of Mount Sinai, perhaps?

definitions.text: Might one wish to warm fingers up

indicators.note: scaling means climbing, so in a down clue the letters read upwards
in means the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A cold climber on Mount Sinai wanting to warm their hands.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer lies within 'Mount Sinai perhaps', running upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard player does finger exercises before performing, so warming up the fingers suits them.

clue.text: Grey has overcome rise of red squirrel

indicators.note: in a down clue, being over something means coming above it

parts.note: hoar means grey or white with age

indicators.note: rise means the colour word reads upwards in a down clue

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Grey squirrels have overcome the red squirrel population.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grey' and 'red' look like squirrel species, but the definition is the verb at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To squirrel things away is to stockpile them, which a person who amasses possessions does.

clue.text: Comedian with run of six characters making comeback, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear tells us the answer sounds like a phrase rather than spelling it

parts.words: run of six characters making comeback
parts.note: six letters counting backwards from P are P, O, N, M, L, K, a run 'P to K'

explanation.surface: A comedian doing a six-character routine and making a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: Running back through the alphabet from P for six letters ends at K, so the run is 'P to K', said aloud like the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Kay is a British stand-up comic from Bolton, known for observational humour.

clue.text: Catholic building in wet field went with the flow, mopping up rug

parts.note: a paddy is a flooded field for growing rice

indicators.note: mopping up means soaking in, so the rug goes inside the past tense of swim

parts.note: swam is what you did when going with a current
rug is slang for a wig or toupee

explanation.surface: Someone drifting through a flooded field in a church, soaking up a rug.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the nickname for Liverpool's Roman Catholic Metropolitan Cathedral, from its conical tent-like shape and the city's Irish heritage.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname is for Liverpool Metropolitan Cathedral, a Roman Catholic church, so a Catholic building.

clue.text: Possible requirement when shifting vehicle to wind power

indicators.note: wind as a verb means twist or turn, so the letters are twisted round

explanation.surface: A vehicle being powered by the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind power' reads as renewable energy, but 'wind' is a verb rearranging the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: A line for towing is needed to pull a broken-down car or other vehicle.

clue.text: Highest nest is one of these things

definitions.text: Highest nest is one of these things

parts.words: Highest nest is one of these things
parts.note: the letters of 'highest nest' rearrange to give 'these things', so it is an example of the kind of wordplay meant

explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like a riddle about birds, but it is self-referential: 'highest nest' and 'these things' use the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A word or phrase formed by rearranging letters of another is exactly what the two phrases are.

clue.text: Some singing 'n' dancing originally in Hollywood film

parts.note: la la la is wordless singing
'n' stands for and, and gives the letter itself

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of dancing

explanation.surface: A musical with singing and dancing, set in Hollywood.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a fair description of the film itself.
explanation.definitionFit: La La Land is the 2016 Hollywood musical starring Ryan Gosling and Emma Stone.

clue.text: See 18 down
Filthy square

definitions.meaning: second meaning: twelve dozen, 144, the square of twelve

explanation.walkthrough: 'square' looks like old-fashioned, but it is the number twelve squared.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means coarse or disgusting, and is also the name for a quantity of 144 items.

clue.text: Royal awards ceremony's ending in hour: Britons had to be decorated

indicators.note: decorated suggests something worked over and made fancy, so the letters are rearranged
ending points to the last letter of the word for the ceremony

explanation.surface: A royal awards ceremony finishing within the hour, with Britons being decorated.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a fair picture of honours being given out.
explanation.definitionFit: These are honours conferred by the monarch each year to mark the official celebration of the sovereign's birth.

clue.text: Article or essay's backing conjecture

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: backing means the back end, so the final letter of essay

explanation.surface: An essay supporting a speculative idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a supposition or hypothesis not yet proven.

clue.text: Rubbish recycling set amid predicament

indicators.note: amid means the reworked letters go in the middle of the word for a fix

parts.note: to be in a jam is to be in a predicament

indicators.note: recycling means reusing material in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Recycling rubbish amid a difficult situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recycling' fits the rubbish picture, but here it is the signal to rearrange the word 'set'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetsam is goods thrown overboard from a ship that wash ashore, hence refuse or junk.
